title: The knot sphere contains Sperner's lemma
claim: The knot sphere contains Sperner's lemma. For m >= 3 and k >= 2m + 4 there is a map from colourings of the side-m triangular grid with a fixed Sperner boundary (corners 0, 1, 2; each side takes its far corner's colour after its first vertex) to assignments of the octahedral knot sphere K_k, each point's colour reading at most two Sperner colours, such that the violated lines of the image lie exactly inside the fully labelled triangles oriented like the boundary: each such triangle holds at least one, oppositely oriented ones hold none. So the one-sided (positive) 2D Sperner problem reduces to finding a violated line, by decision trees of depth at most two, and any query or resolution-width lower bound for it transfers to K_k. Moreover, for Sperner states, pebbled colours admit a state whose only full triangle is a given T iff an integer difference system on pebble sheets has no negative cycle; an obstruction between two positions needs a closed walk through pebbles that separates them with free-segment excess sum (len - 2) at most |forced winding| + 3|winding| + 2.
failure_conditions: A coarse triangle colouring that is not fully labelled with the boundary's orientation but contains a violated fine line, or a positively oriented one containing none.
A Sperner colouring whose image violates a line outside R, on its boundary, or inside a triangle that is not fully labelled with the boundary's orientation.
A point of K_k whose image colour depends on more than two Sperner colours.
A pebbled colouring and triangle on which the difference-system criterion and the solver disagree.
foundation_claim_scope: Sperner grids of side 3..6 inside K_{2m+4} (exhaustive for side <= 5, 3000 random colourings at side 6); the local lemma exhaustively in the bulk lattice; the window criterion on grids of side 5..7.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: the reduction and local lemma by hand plus exhaustive or sampled computation; the window criterion by the standard difference-constraint argument plus solver comparison; no human or external review
validation.novelty: new as far as found: Sperner's lemma, its PPAD reading and its query and tree-like resolution bounds are classical (Crescenzi-Silvestri; Itsykson-Malova-Oparin-Sokolov 2014); the delta is that the knot's Euler count on the sphere contains the one-sided 2D Sperner problem by a depth-two decision-tree reduction, with the six corner disclinations playing the Sperner boundary.
